question: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the compound interest, when interest is compounded 6-monthly, and the simple interest on a sum of Rs. 20,000 for 1(1)/(2) year at 10% p.a.?
solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 20,000

Rate = 10%

Time = 1(1)/(2) years = 3/2 years​​​​

**Formula used:**

A = P (1 + r/100)t

SI = (P × R × T)/100

**Calculation:**

If Interest is compounded 6-monthly, then

Rate = 10/2 = 5%

Time = 3/2 × 2 = 3 years

Now,

Amount = 20,000 × (1 + 5/100)³

⇒ (20,000 × 21/20 × 21/20 × 21/20)

⇒ Rs. 23,152.5

CI = (23,152.5 – 20,000)

⇒ Rs. 3,152.5

SI = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ [(20,000 × 10 × 3/2) × 100]

⇒ Rs. 3000

Required difference = (3152.5 – 3000)

⇒ 152.5

**∴ The required difference is 152.5 **
